cases.given: An authoritative project plan has one current lifecycle-tracked item whose outcome is a small calculator behavior change.
expect: Keep one lifecycle-tracked item for the behavior-complete outcome.
Put implementation and verification order in subordinate steps or acceptance evidence.
Do not create separate planning, coding, testing, review, or documentation items.

cases.given: A migration has independently resumable schema, compatibility, and rollout outcomes with dependencies.
expect: Use separate lifecycle-tracked items for the independently resumable acceptance boundaries.
Keep subordinate commands and checks inside each owning item.
Preserve the authoritative project plan as the only planning state.

cases.given: A small code change has no project-owned plan or decision-record system and does not need durable planning state.
expect: Use the runtime's own lightweight planning only when the task needs it.
Do not create a repository plan, decision log, or other durable process artifact.
Implement and validate the requested observable behavior directly.

cases.given: A new 700-line checkout feature has no project conventions yet and combines pricing rules, payment API calls, database writes, and HTTP handlers in one proposed file.
expect: Identify the existing pricing, payment, persistence and delivery responsibilities from their contracts, not from the line count.
Use the smallest coherent set of purpose-named modules that keeps domain rules, external I/O, persistence, and delivery responsibilities independently navigable.
Do not prescribe a named architecture, speculative layer, empty directory, or one-function-file pattern.

cases.given: An established project organizes functional modules by feature, returns error tuples, and colocates tests, but one legacy API helper logs access tokens. A new change could instead be written with the agent's preferred class-based layered architecture.
expect: Follow the project's feature boundaries, functional idioms, error handling, naming, and colocated test style without copying the unsafe token logging.
Do not transplant the preferred class-based layered architecture merely because it appears more modern.
Depart from a local convention only when required for the requested outcome, safety, or a binding contract.

cases.given: A 2100-line hand-written protocol grammar has one coherent responsibility and a required format whose split would break a validated invariant. The project has no stricter configured limit.
expect: Preserve the coherent file and its validated invariant without requesting a size exception.
Do not split, compress, or rename fragments merely because of the line count.
Validate the requested behavior through the existing contract.

cases.given: A Testing Library failure prints the same large DOM snapshot on two consecutive attempts.
expect: Retain the first complete diagnostic once.
On repetition report the stable failure signature and meaningful delta only.
Inspect the focused source owner before editing again.

cases.given: A generated 24000-line source snapshot names its generator. The requested behavior change belongs in the generator input.
expect: Change the generator or its hand-written input, not the generated snapshot.
Do not split generated output to satisfy the line limit.
Regenerate and validate the affected artifact through the existing project workflow.

cases.given: A hand-written 2400-line module has several responsibilities. The proposed fix only renames it to part-1 and part-2 files while retaining shared globals and bidirectional calls.
expect: Reject the numbered split because it preserves coupling and obscures ownership.
Use a real responsibility boundary if the requested refactor requires a split; no size exception is needed.
Do not compress code or delete useful comments to pass the metric.

cases.given: A focused security fix touches five lines in a coherent 2300-line legacy parser. No safe responsibility split is established by the task evidence.
expect: Apply and validate the narrow security fix without expanding it into an unrequested refactor.
Keep security ahead of the maintainability signal.
Do not report the file size itself as an unresolved defect or require a separate refactor.

cases.given: A project adds a real customer-data import adapter and also adds ordinary language import statements to three existing modules.
expect: Place the data-import behavior in its existing project owner or an actual responsibility boundary; require no dedicated directory solely because it imports data.
Keep ordinary language import statements with their consuming modules under project conventions.
Create no directory per import statement and no empty plugin or adapter scaffolding.

cases.given: A large module was split into named domain files and all files compile. The old canonical entry point does not import or register the new modules, so the split behavior is absent at startup.
expect: Do not treat compilation as proof that the split works.
Repair the one canonical import, autoload, registration, or startup path so every required new module is reachable.
Exercise startup and affected consumers, preserve boundary semantics, and create no duplicate loader.

cases.given: The full suite passed, then a new regression test and related production fix were added.
expect: Treat the earlier aggregate pass as stale for the late change.
Rerun the smallest aggregate check covering the changed code and test, or narrow the completion claim.
Do not cite the earlier suite as proof of the new behavior.

cases.given: A newline correction deduplicates separators in one conversion path. Inspection shows that the same operation can collapse blank lines in unchanged text.
expect: Inspect the blank-line variant through the demonstrated shared cause and validate its preserved text behavior.
Correct the conversion mechanism rather than adding a special case for the reported string.
Do not expand into a full parser redesign or unrelated input combinations.

cases.given: A layout correction preserves a selected occurrence ID. On the same layout transition, the focused card may replace the selected card while the old occurrence ID survives.
expect: Inspect whether the retained occurrence belongs to the card selected by the affected transition.
Check the visible card and navigation selection together through that transition.
Keep the existing state owner and avoid introducing a global state framework.

cases.given: The directly exposed variants have decisive passing regression evidence against the final changed code. No related code or tests changed afterward and no separate risk remains.
expect: Reuse the current evidence for the covered variants.
Add no duplicate test, fixed test quota, or unchanged rerun solely to demonstrate thoroughness.

cases.given: A nearby legacy function has a similar name to the corrected function but the evidence establishes no shared cause, dependency, changed public contract, or affected behavior.
expect: Keep inspection and correction within the evidenced contract.
Do not repair the neighboring function or infer an affected consumer from its name or location.

cases.given: An editor mock returns the initial HTML unchanged. The required acceptance concerns actual editor initialization normalizing that HTML without marking untouched content dirty. The actual editor is available locally.
expect: Exercise initialization with the actual editor and observe the dirty state.
Do not treat the mock pass as normalization evidence.
If the actual check cannot run, report that boundary as unverified and leave its required acceptance open.

cases.given: A cache-read test globally fails storage, so the preceding state read fails first. A proposed relaxation accepts either state-error or cache-error while both paths avoid the provider. A separate negative test already returns an unambiguous error from its named operation.
expect: Make the state read succeed and inject failure only at the cache read before claiming cache-error coverage.
Keep the state-read failure separately proven and verify the relevant no-provider aftermath for both paths.
Reject accepting both error codes as target-path proof and do not add counters or production instrumentation to the already unambiguous control.

cases.given: A deterministic text transformation runs directly on controlled input strings. Acceptance is limited to that transformation; no dependency behavior or producer-consumer compatibility is claimed.
expect: Accept decisive direct checks as evidence for the transformation.
Do not require a browser, live service, or integration test solely because the inputs are fixtures.

cases.given: A renderer test supplies a hand-written object containing an expected adapter label. Required acceptance also includes compatibility between the real adapter output and renderer input.
expect: Exercise the actual producer-consumer boundary with controlled source data.
Do not treat the prepared label or renderer-only pass as evidence that adapter extraction works.
Keep the required compatibility condition open until that boundary has evidence.

cases.given: A producer and its green unit test both use `title.font.font.size`, while an independently specified local consumer and its actual implementation accept only `title.font.size`. A separate deterministic string transformation has no integration claim.
expect: Derive the boundary expectation from the independent contract or actual consumer rather than the producer test.
Correct the producer and its mirrored expectation without changing the consumer contract.
Exercise the actual consumer and retain the direct pure-transformation check without requiring browser, network, or framework integration.

cases.given: A required integration boundary cannot be exercised locally, and the only available external route lacks user authorization. Mock results cover only the local request builder.
expect: Report the request-builder evidence separately from the unverified integration boundary.
Respect existing permissions and request only the missing authorization if dependent work requires it.
Do not start the external action or mark the unmet acceptance complete.

cases.given: Findings after two consecutive correction attempts use different input strings and check names, but each confirms that the same conversion still discards significant separators. Existing regression checks pass.
expect: Stop patching and re-read the responsible implementation, contract, and evidence before another correction.
Change the approach or narrow the change without weakening required acceptance.
Different reproductions, fresh failure output and passing existing checks do not reset the two-unsuccessful-corrections checkpoint.

cases.given: Two findings occur in the same file. One is a text conversion defect and the other is an unrelated permission check; the evidence shows distinct causal mechanisms.
expect: Diagnose each finding through its actual owner and risk.
Do not combine unrelated failures into the same repair checkpoint merely because of their count or location.
Preserve the security requirements of the permission defect.

cases.given: Only one correction attempt has failed. Its new evidence identifies a bounded cause, required permissions are present, and no host limit prevents the next correction.
expect: Use the new evidence for the next focused correction and proportionate checks.
Do not claim the two-correction checkpoint has been reached or wait for a second failure before using a supported diagnosis.

cases.given: Repeated verified failures require cause diagnosis, but the host's correction allowance is exhausted. A fallback may be used only if already authorized.
expect: Respect the exhausted allowance while diagnosing or reporting the remaining cause.
Use only an existing authorized fallback, otherwise leave the dependent work incomplete.
Do not create another attempt or conversation or infer permission from the diagnostic rule.

cases.given: A contained internal code change has no changed public symbol or contract. Inspection establishes the owner, affected behavior, and sufficient focused evidence, with no directly exposed additional variant.
expect: Stop exploration at the established owner and evidence boundary.
Do not inspect consumers or create variant tests as insurance.
Preserve the existing consumer requirement when a different task actually changes a symbol or public behavior.

cases.given: An explicit formatter contract change affects two distinct consumers registered in a local registry and an old formatter test double. An unrelated neighboring module has a similar name. A separate internal rewrite preserves its contract.
expect: Locate and update both independently affected registered consumer variants and the test double.
Exercise both variants through focused tests and leave the unrelated neighbor unchanged.
Do not require a consumer inventory for the separate internal rewrite whose contract is unchanged.

cases.given: An isolated repository names a small configuration change and one result field in an explicitly required large single-line JSONL source, alongside 500 irrelevant files. The possible content scope is otherwise broad.
expect: Select candidate paths and bound returned output before reading file contents.
Edit only the named configuration and filter the large JSONL source locally to the requested field.
Do not recursively dump irrelevant contents or automatically drain truncated output.

cases.given: A request names one exact small configuration file and requires a contained value change with no evidence implicating other paths.
expect: Read the named small file directly and apply the contained change.
Do not add a directory, size, or repository inventory as a prerequisite.

cases.given: The user requests review of the implementation and test evidence after two corrections fail through the same conversion mechanism across different checks. No plan change or unresolved product decision is requested.
expect: Load Change for the implementation review and Validation for evidence and repeated-failure assessment.
Select references from implementation and evidence work actually reviewed, regardless of whether the failures came from the same check.
Do not add Planning or new workflow requirements solely because the failure repeated.

cases.given: Documented setup and an alternate check failed to exercise a required integration. The needed service is now demonstrably restored.
expect: Rerun the narrow required check because relevant conditions changed.
Keep required acceptance open until actual evidence passes.

cases.given: All affected behavior and risks have decisive evidence. Inputs and environment are unchanged and no binding protocol requires repetition.
expect: Stop checking.
Do not justify identical repetition merely because residual risk is nonzero.

cases.given: After the final scoped diff inspection an authorized concurrent source change alters affected behavior.
expect: Inspect the changed final tree and validate the affected behavior.
Do not cite stale evidence or treat the earlier final inspection as a ban on necessary checks.

cases.given: The user explicitly replaced an ordinary product rule. An old assertion now contradicts that authorized rule and no security guarantee is removed.
expect: Update the obsolete assertion to the authorized new contract.
Prove the new behavior and preserve remaining guarantees.

cases.given: A security guard fails in a bugfix. Deleting it makes existing checks pass. The user has not authorized dropping that guarantee.
expect: Preserve the guard and fix the actual cause.
Do not infer authority to drop a guarantee from a general bugfix request.

cases.given: Initialize a wholly new Angular application. No project naming or layout requirements are present.
expect: Read project-conventions.md after checking project instructions and existing organization.
Use Angular feature organization and hyphenated filenames with colocated spec tests.
Do not force a generic central tests directory or development wrapper.

cases.given: Initialize a wholly new Python project whose AGENTS.md prescribes a source folder and filename convention compatible with Python.
expect: Apply project requirements first.
Use the Greenfield reference only for choices not already prescribed.

cases.given: An established application gains a module in a newly created empty directory.
expect: Do not load or apply project-conventions.md.
Follow the existing project organization and conventions.

cases.given: An established application has no explicit naming rule for a requested new source file.
expect: Do not activate the Greenfield fallback because an individual rule is missing.
Use established surrounding code and applicable project requirements.

cases.given: A wholly new project has applicable AGENTS.md explicitly directing an unreadable personal conventions file. Project-specific requirements are readable.
expect: Report the exact unavailable path and stop only dependent organization choices.
Continue independent authorized work under known project requirements.
Do not silently replace required personal instructions with bundled defaults.

cases.given: A wholly new WordPress plugin uses Composer PSR-4 for its namespaced classes.
expect: Honor the actual PSR-4 loading contract and case-matching namespace paths.
Use WordPress filename conventions where applicable without breaking PSR-4-loaded classes.

cases.given: A DB integration check remains blocked by unchanged infrastructure. One alternative syntax check passed but did not establish preservation of status/reason/error/source. An existing isolated serializer contract test needs no DB and can answer that named open acceptance question.
expect: Run the targeted serializer contract test despite an earlier alternative and unchanged infrastructure.
Do not retry the unchanged blocked integration check or claim integration was verified.

cases.given: Plan a new reporting subproject within an established repository that uses app/ and tests/ with snake_case modules.
expect: Preserve applicable repository requirements and observed organization.
Do not load project-conventions.md for a new subproject inside the existing repository.

cases.given: Refactor an established shipping module without changing behavior.
expect: Preserve the current organization and names and validate the affected behavior.
Do not load or apply the Greenfield project-conventions.md reference.

cases.given: A new project refers to docs/project-conventions.md from its root AGENTS.md while the shell starts in a different directory.
expect: Resolve the relative reference from the AGENTS.md directory, not the shell working directory.
Read only the explicitly directed file, without personal-file discovery.

cases.given: A developer CLI reads a required JSON config through read_text and json.loads. Missing or malformed input already aborts visibly before any writes. Internal functions receive immutable values whose relevant properties the caller guarantees.
expect: Use the existing failure paths; add no redundant existence checks, catch-and-rethrow, or internal validation of guaranteed properties.
Preserve any separately required actionable error contract.

cases.given: One endpoint accepts raw JSON and promises a dictionary, but only has a dict return annotation. After actual boundary validation, fields pass into a pure function. A separate filesystem path can be replaced by another process after validation and before a destructive operation.
expect: Reject non-object JSON at the input boundary; a return annotation is not validation. Rely on unchanged validated properties internally.
Do not treat stale path validation as proof of safe deletion; preserve protection at the destructive boundary.

cases.given: One change to an internal typed helper fails visibly on unsupported input without side effects. A separate change catches a failed save and reports success. Review both.
expect: Do not block the helper for lacking defensive checks; omit optional ideas unless relevant to a decision.
Report the false save success as a defect with its actual consequence and smallest correction.

cases.given: A root-cause correction fixes the actual parse defect after earlier attempts added a retry and a None guard. Neither still protects a requirement or material consequence. An independent authorization guard is still required.
expect: Remove the now-unjustified retry and None guard from the changed path.
Preserve the authorization guard; an unsuccessful attempt alone does not justify deleting protection.

cases.given: A CLI already has useful generated output when an optional delivery step fails. Keeping that output is permitted. No restart or durable recovery contract exists.
expect: Preserve the available output and report the delivery failure without claiming completion.
Do not add checkpoints, a recovery command, or persisted execution state solely for manual recovery.

cases.given: A worker adds retries around parsing an immutable local manifest, although malformed input already fails visibly without writes and no transient failure or retry contract exists. A separate idempotent service adapter must retry TimeoutError up to three total attempts under its existing contract, then propagate the final failure.
expect: Report the manifest retry as an unnecessary repeated operation with extra branches and no transient recovery benefit; remove only that retry.
Preserve the service adapter retry required by its contract and its visible final failure; do not turn a preference for fewer retries into a finding.

cases.given: One input contract supplies a flat sequence of form fields. Another requires arbitrarily nested child groups. Both need selected values in source order.
expect: Use direct traversal for flat fields without recursively searching unrelated objects.
Support actual nesting for the tree contract; a blanket recursion ban is incorrect.

cases.given: An unreleased prototype replaces format 1 with format 2. The user explicitly authorizes regenerating its disposable fixtures and supporting only format 2.
expect: Implement format 2 and update actual consumers and fixtures.
Add no legacy parser, migration registry or second approval request.

cases.given: A requested format change would make saved customer records unreadable. The task does not settle continued support or migration.
expect: Ask the concrete support or migration question before the dependent change.
Do not silently discard the records, add fallback parsing, or infer that prerelease status removes existing data obligations.

cases.given: One consumer uses a parser with an existing input contract and parser-owned state. A bounded refactor can isolate that responsibility without generic extension points.
expect: Allow useful encapsulation with one consumer.
Require no fabricated second consumer, generic factory or configurable parser family.

cases.given: A patch satisfies the stated contract with two straightforward linear passes, no repeated I/O and no demonstrated material cost. An alternative could combine the passes with more state.
expect: Accept the patch without a finding based solely on pass count.
Do not request the alternative or invent a performance requirement.

cases.given: The requirement says integer discounts use floor(total * percent / 100). The implementation and its test both round to nearest instead, while a correct control handles floor.
expect: Derive expectations from the specified floor rule and correct the faulty calculation and mirrored assertion.
Preserve the correct control and require no additional test framework.

cases.given: A request-local result store avoids repeated pure calculations on immutable inputs within an already authorized implementation. It adds no external effects or material cost or behavior choice.
expect: Assess its actual benefit and lifetime, then decide locally.
Do not require a cache-specific user approval or invent invalidation machinery.

cases.given: Two wholly new projects have no layout requirements and their toolchains allow the Skill defaults. One currently needs source and tests, the other also needs development scripts.
expect: Use the same src/tests/docs/scripts base where content exists, respecting toolchain naming.
Create no empty directories; preserve the user-selected consistency convention without claiming a measured correctness benefit.

cases.given: The user explicitly requests a transfer of a code task with a user-owned dirty file, a running command with an unknown exit, and no publication authority. In one variant Scoville Handoff is active. In another, Code is installed alone and Handoff is unavailable.
expect: With active Handoff, preserve its full continuation contract, including Receiver Instructions, ownership, hazards, evidence limits and Resume Steps. Code's engineering-state summary must not restrict that prompt.

Without Handoff, Code prepares the requested handoff from the outcome, binding constraints, current state, decisive evidence, next concrete step and material decisions not already recorded canonically. Do not require, install or simulate Handoff or create a new record system.
In both variants, preserve the user-owned change, unknown command exit and missing publication authority without continuing implementation or claiming unobserved success.

cases.given: A parser with one consumer and one required format can have its state encapsulated directly. A proposed refactor also adds a parser registry, abstract strategy and factory for unspecified future formats.
expect: Allow the existing responsibility to be encapsulated without requiring a second consumer.
Reject the registry, abstract strategy and factory because no current format or consumer needs those extra variants; preserve the direct parser boundary.

cases.given: Two corrections have failed to fix separator loss. Each run printed a different failing input and old regression checks stayed green. The agent proposes a third string-specific patch based only on that fresh output.
expect: Reassess the owner, contract and causal evidence before another patch; the two-correction checkpoint still applies.
Treat new output as useful for a next attempt only if it changes or substantiates the causal explanation; add no unsupported special case.

cases.given: A small fixed-size form performs one remote lookup per field although the same required result can be fetched once. A separate patch scans a tiny local list twice without plausible material cost.
expect: Assess the repeated remote I/O even though the form cannot grow, and compare the existing shared fetch.
Do not demand a benchmark or complex one-pass rewrite for the tiny local list merely because it has two traversals.
